correctness.rationale: The circulant entry S=N*P_0j uses a single Nyquist cosine on even grids and symmetric Fourier modes through (N-1)/2 on odd grids. The full Poisson-periodized Gaussian Theta is positive. Write c=Nt, d=N/2-j with 0<=j<=floor(N/2), and phi(c)=(c-pi²/c)/4. In the odd omitted tail, frequency (N+1)/2+l has nodal cosine (-1)^(j+l) sin(2pi*d*(l+1/2)/N), since (N/2)x=pi*j. This gives a geometrically summable multiplier d/N absent in the even bound. Using the nearest Gaussian image, the tail/Gaussian ratio on pi/2<=c<=2pi is bounded by a constant times N^-1/2 times exp(-N*phi(c)) on even grids, or N^-3/2 times that exponential on odd grids: one uses x²/(4t)-N²t/4 <= -N*phi(c)-pi²*d/(2c), so the factor d is uniformly absorbed on the compact c range. At c_plus=pi-(kappa*log N-B)/N, N*phi=-kappa*log N/2+B/2+o(1), with phi increasing. This proves strict positivity up to c=2pi when B is sufficiently large. For 2pi<=c<=2N the geometric prefactors and d/N are bounded, sqrt(t)<=sqrt(2) and phi(c)>=phi(2pi)>0. For t>=2 the constant mode exceeds the sum of all nonconstant magnitudes. Thus the upper bound is for every later real time. For the lower bound choose j=2*floor(N/4), hence d=0,1 (even) or 1/2,3/2 (odd). The two nearest Gaussian images together give a positive constant multiple of sqrt(N)*exp(-pi²*N/(4c)) uniformly when c→pi. At that even j, geometric domination gives the positive even tail factor tanh(c/2); the scaled odd linearized sine sum is sum_l (l+1/2)(-exp(-c))^l=(1-exp(-c))/(2(1+exp(-c))²)>0. The odd factor d/N survives because d is bounded away from zero. The resulting Gaussian/tail ratio at c_minus=pi-(kappa*log N+B)/N is a bounded positive prefactor times exp(-B/2)(1+o(1)), below one for sufficiently large fixed B. A negative entry there and the uniform upper positivity yield the stated bracketing and O(N^-2) error. Independent 220-digit replay at B=12 covered N=100–103, 128–131, 200–203, 256–259 and all upper-time entries. For N=100 and 101 the scaled lower witnesses were approximately -4.4500e-33 and -1.3949e-34; upper minima were 9.3425e-33 and 1.1275e-33. Replay: python3 /workspace/reviews/evidence/4-heat-check.py (mpmath). This finite arithmetic neither proves the asymptotic nor certifies positivity at all subsequent times; the analytical envelope does. Frozen verifier inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: For an unmodified spectral heat discretization, exact preservation of the nonnegative nodal cone is stronger than near-contractivity. The sharp leading odd law and its factor-three logarithmic advance resolve a parity-dependent sign effect at a physically motivated threshold, while uniform all-later-time positivity makes the claim about the last occurrence of negativity rather than a sampled sign. No exact finite-grid root or off-grid positivity is claimed.
